seo.metaTitle: Add Noise to PNG - Film Grain In Your Browser
seo.metaDescription: Add monochrome or color noise to an image in your browser. The grain is deterministic by seed, so the same settings always give the same picture. Free, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Add noise sprinkles grain over the picture, the way film stock adds texture and older digital cameras add luminance noise in low light. Monochrome grain changes the brightness of each pixel and leaves its hue alone, which keeps a color palette intact; color noise shifts all three channels, which looks more like a broken sensor. The result is deterministic — the same seed always produces exactly the same grain, so a look can be reproduced later instead of being a lucky roll of the dice. The effect is applied in your browser, and the image is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Monochrome keeps the color palette; color noise shifts all three channels.
Deterministic by seed: the same settings always give the same picture.
Noise hides detail visually but does not remove it from the file.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Choose the noise type: monochrome keeps the color palette, color shifts hue as well.
Set the amount: a light grain is a texture, a heavy one hides the picture.
Note the seed if you like the result, so the same grain can be reproduced later.

faq.q: What is the difference between monochrome and color noise?
faq.a: Monochrome grain adds a random amount of brightness to each pixel and leaves red, green and blue in their original proportion, so the colors of the picture stay as they were. Color noise changes the channels independently, which adds a colored speckle and pulls the palette apart.

faq.q: Why does the same image look the same twice?
faq.a: Because the noise is generated from the seed, not at random. The same seed and the same amount always give the same grain, which is what makes a result repeatable.

faq.q: Can noise hide information in a photo?
faq.a: It can hide detail visually, but it does not remove it from the file: the pixels are still there underneath. Never treat noise as a way to anonymize a photo.
No. The grain is generated and applied in your browser tab, so your file stays on your device and nothing is stored.
